A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ERTACache. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and matchable despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original image/video generation experiments, component ablations, calibration-size sensitivity results, and memory/latency measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results in Tables 1–4 and the main-text and appendix figures.

M1.justification: Offline policy calibration, trajectory-aware timestep adjustment and residual error rectification remain unchanged. Equations 12–21 and Algorithms 1–2 specify the same procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate image/video generation using Open-Sora 1.2, CogVideoX, Wan2.1 and Flux-dev 1.0. VBench evaluation and the appendix analysis using 1,000 MS COCO 2014 examples are retained without new task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within each experiment: Tables 1–2 retain the same combinations of Delta-DiT, T-GATE, PAB, FasterCache, TeaCache and ProfilingDiT. Table 4 retains the same memory/latency comparators.

E3.justification: The reported metrics, sampling-step budgets, frame counts, resolutions, VBench prompts, disabled prompt extension and baseline-default settings are unchanged. The omitted prompt-count disclosure does not establish a changed experiment.

E4.justification: The component ablations, calibration-size sensitivity analysis, memory/latency comparison and cache-error visualizations are retained. The added paragraph in v2 Section 4.3 points to analyses already present in v1's supplement.

E5.justification: Both report five videos per prompt with distinct random seeds and single-video, seed-0 ablations. The plotted variability and statistical reporting practices are unchanged; no uncertainty-estimation procedure or statistical test is added.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain identical results, and the corresponding plots and qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, Wan2.1 ERTACache retains 2.17× speedup, 80.73% VBench and 23.77 PSNR in Table 1.

T1.justification: The error-accumulation derivation and residual-linearization mathematics, including appendix Equations 22–35, are unchanged apart from punctuation and typesetting. No assumptions, proofs or mathematical corrections are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same error decomposition, three-component caching contribution, and acceleration-with-preserved-quality claims. The new disclosure sections do not redefine the scientific contributions.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations, speed–quality tradeoffs and interpretations of generalization and overhead remain unchanged. The new main-text sensitivity summary repeats existing supplementary interpretations; no substantive technical limitation is added.

D1.justification: v1's explicit ERTACache code URL is removed. v2 Section 7 instead claims public code and datasets in an anonymous repository without identifying it. The merged Figure 2 caption also omits v1's specification of 10 diverse prompts; other implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: The cited research works and positioning relative to previous caching methods are unchanged. Citation styling and bibliographic presentation change without adding research references or revising novelty arguments.

P1.justification: v2 adds ethics, reproducibility and LLM-use statements, numbers existing sections, updates author order and citation styling, and lightly edits appendix prose. The scientific narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The two-column main text is comprehensively reset into a single-column conference layout, changing typography, margins, headers and figure/table placement. v1 Figures 2 and 3 become v2 Figure 2(a,b); later figures are renumbered and resized while retaining their content.

improvement.justification: Scientific evidence is preserved, and numbered sections and new disclosures offer modest benefits. However, removing the explicit code URL and Figure 2's 10-prompt count weakens reproducibility reporting. Section 7's unlinked anonymous-repository assertion does not restore that actionable information.
